questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) II, IV, I, III. अभिकथन (A): सोलहवीं सदी के मध्य तक आते-आते पुर्तगाली और स्पेनिश सेनाओं की विजय का सिलसिला शुरू हो चुका था तथा उन्होंने अमेरिका को उपनिवेश बनाना शुरू कर दिया था।
कारण (R): स्पेनिश विजेताओं के पास सबसे शक्तिशाली परंपरागत हथियार थे।
questions.text_english:
Two statements labelled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): The Portuguese and Spanish conquest and colonisation of America was decisively under way by the mid-sixteenth century.
Reason (R): The Spanish conquerors had the most powerful conventional weapons.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. The Assertion is historically accurate — by the mid-sixteenth century, the Portuguese and Spanish had indeed begun colonising the Americas decisively. However, the Reason is false because the Spanish conquerors did not prevail due to superior conventional weapons alone. Their success was primarily due to the germs they carried (smallpox and other diseases) which decimated the indigenous population, along with political and military strategies. The Reason thus misrepresents the key cause of Spanish conquest.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। अभिकथन सत्य है क्योंकि सोलहवीं सदी के मध्य तक स्पेनिश और पुर्तगाली अमेरिका को उपनिवेश बना चुके थे। परंतु कारण असत्य है क्योंकि उनकी विजय का मुख्य कारण परंपरागत हथियार नहीं, बल्कि उनके साथ आई बीमारियाँ (जैसे चेचक) थीं जिन्होंने स्थानीय जनसंख्या को बड़े पैमाने पर नष्ट कर दिया।

questions.text_english:
Choose the correct option to fill in the blank.
The Indus Valley Civilization was linked to the _______ region through coastal trade as early as 3000 BCE.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) West Asia. Archaeological and historical evidence shows that as early as 3000 BCE, the Indus Valley Civilization had active coastal trade links with West Asia (including Mesopotamia). Trade goods such as cotton textiles, beads, and precious stones moved between the two regions. North America, South America, and South Australia had no known trade connections with the Indus Valley Civilization at that time.

questions.text_english:
(a) Analyse Gutenberg's contribution to printing in Europe.
OR
(b) "Printing is the ultimate gift of God and the greatest one." Analyse the statement.
questions.instruction_line: केवल एक प्रश्न का उत्तर लिखें।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer only one of the two options.

key_points: Gutenberg developed the printing press with movable type around 1448 in Strasbourg.
He adapted the screw press used in wine and olive presses to create the printing press.
He used lead alloy for creating movable type, oil-based ink, and durable paper.
His first major work was the Bible — about 180 copies printed between 1450–1455.
This revolutionised book production, reduced costs, and democratised knowledge across Europe.

questions.solution:
Johannes Gutenberg developed the first mechanical printing press with movable type around 1448 in Strasbourg, Europe. He was inspired by the screw press used in wine and olive oil industries and adapted it to create a printing machine. He used an oil-based ink that stuck well to metal type, and combined it with a durable paper and a metal alloy for letters. His first major printed work was the Bible, of which around 180 copies were printed between 1450 and 1455. Before Gutenberg, books were hand-copied, making them rare and expensive. His invention dramatically reduced the cost and time of book production, making knowledge accessible to a wider population. It sparked the spread of new ideas, the Protestant Reformation, and eventually the Scientific Revolution across Europe. Gutenberg's press is thus considered one of the most transformative inventions in human history.

OR

Martin Luther's famous statement, "Printing is the ultimate gift of God and the greatest one," reflects the profound impact of print technology on religious and intellectual life. The printing press enabled the rapid spread of Luther's Ninety-Five Theses in 1517, translating a local protest against the Church into a continent-wide Reformation movement within weeks. Print allowed the Bible to be translated into vernacular languages and made available to ordinary people, breaking the Church's monopoly over religious interpretation. It empowered individuals to read and interpret scriptures themselves, leading to the Protestant Reformation. Print also helped spread new scientific ideas, political philosophies, and literary works. Luther correctly identified print as a divine tool because it democratised knowledge, challenged authority, and transformed European society fundamentally.
questions.solution_hindi: जोहान्स गुटेन्बर्ग ने लगभग 1448 में यूरोप के स्ट्रासबर्ग में पहली यांत्रिक मुद्रण प्रेस विकसित की। उन्होंने शराब और जैतून के तेल उद्योग में उपयोग होने वाले स्क्रू प्रेस से प्रेरणा लेकर मुद्रण यंत्र बनाया। उनकी पहली महत्वपूर्ण मुद्रित कृति बाइबल थी। इस आविष्कार ने ज्ञान को सुलभ बनाया, धर्म-सुधार आंदोलन को बढ़ावा दिया और यूरोपीय समाज को मूल रूप से बदल दिया।

questions.text:
(क) 1789 में फ्रांसीसी क्रांति को राष्ट्रवाद की पहली स्पष्ट अभिव्यक्ति क्यों माना जाता है? उदाहरणों सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) साम्राज्यवाद से जुड़कर राष्ट्रवाद किस प्रकार 1914 में यूरोप को महाविपदा की ओर ले गया? उदाहरणों सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Why is the French Revolution of 1789 considered the first clear expression of nationalism? Explain with examples.
OR
(b) How did nationalism, aligned with imperialism, lead Europe to disaster in 1914? Explain with examples.
questions.instruction_line: केवल एक प्रश्न का उत्तर लिखें।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer only one of the two options.

key_points: The French Revolution transferred sovereignty from the monarchy to the French citizens/nation.
New ideas such as la patrie (the fatherland) and le citoyen (the citizen) emphasized a unified national identity.
The National Assembly replaced the Estates General, signifying power to the people.
A new French flag (tricolour) replaced the royal standard.
Revolutionary armies spread nationalist ideas to other European nations.

questions.solution:
The French Revolution of 1789 is considered the first clear expression of nationalism because it fundamentally redefined the concept of political power and identity. Before the Revolution, France was a monarchy where all power resided in the king. The Revolution transferred sovereignty from the monarch to the French nation — the people became the source of all political authority. New political concepts such as 'la patrie' (the fatherland) and 'le citoyen' (the citizen) were introduced, creating a sense of collective national identity. The Estates General was replaced by the National Assembly, symbolizing representative governance. A new tricolour flag replaced the royal standard, and new national hymns were composed. The metric system was adopted as a unifying national standard. Revolutionary armies carried these ideas beyond French borders. When French armies marched into other European territories, they spread the message of liberty, equality, and national self-determination. This inspired nationalistic movements across Europe, making the French Revolution the starting point of modern European nationalism.

OR

Nationalism aligned with imperialism led Europe to disaster in 1914 through a combination of intense national rivalries, imperial competition, and militarism. By the late nineteenth century, European nations were competing aggressively for colonies in Asia and Africa, creating bitter rivalries. Germany, Austria-Hungary, and the Ottoman Empire formed the Triple Alliance, while Britain, France, and Russia formed the Triple Entente, dividing Europe into two armed camps. The Balkan region became a hotbed of nationalist tensions, particularly as Slavic peoples sought independence from Austro-Hungarian rule. When Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria was assassinated in Sarajevo in June 1914 by a Serbian nationalist, it triggered a chain reaction due to the alliance system. Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, Russia mobilized to support Serbia, Germany declared war on Russia and France, and Britain entered the war when Germany invaded Belgium. Nationalist propaganda fuelled public support for the war in every country. The result was the First World War, the most catastrophic conflict Europe had seen — millions died, empires collapsed, and the continent was devastated.
questions.solution_hindi: 1789 की फ्रांसीसी क्रांति को राष्ट्रवाद की पहली स्पष्ट अभिव्यक्ति माना जाता है क्योंकि इसने राजनीतिक शक्ति की अवधारणा को बदल दिया। राजशाही की जगह 'राष्ट्र' को संप्रभु बनाया गया। 'ला पात्री' और 'ले सिटोएन' जैसी नई अवधारणाएँ सामने आईं। एस्टेट्स जनरल की जगह राष्ट्रीय सभा बनी। फ्रांसीसी सेनाओं ने ये विचार यूरोप भर में फैलाए, जिससे आधुनिक राष्ट्रवाद का जन्म हुआ।

questions.text:
दिए गए स्रोत को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर लिखिए:

भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन

क्रिप्स मिशन की असफलता एवं द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के प्रभावों ने भारत में व्यापक असंतोष को जन्म दिया। इसके फलस्वरूप गाँधीजी ने एक आंदोलन शुरू किया, जिसमें उन्होंने अंग्रेजों के पूरी तरह से भारत छोड़ने पर जोर दिया। वर्धा में 14 जुलाई 1942 को अपनी कार्यकारिणी में काँग्रेस कार्य समिति ने ऐतिहासिक 'भारत छोड़ो' प्रस्ताव पारित किया, जिसमें सत्ता का भारतीयों को तत्काल हस्तांतरण एवं भारत छोड़ने की माँग की गई। 8 अगस्त 1942 को बंबई में अखिल भारतीय काँग्रेस समिति ने इस प्रस्ताव का समर्थन किया, जिसमें पूरे देश में व्यापक पैमाने पर एक अहिंसक जन संघर्ष का आह्वान किया गया। इसी अवसर पर गाँधीजी ने प्रसिद्ध 'करो या मरो' भाषण दिया था। 'भारत छोड़ो' के इस आह्वान ने देश के अधिकतर हिस्सों में राज्य व्यवस्था को ठप्प कर दिया, लोग स्वत: ही आंदोलन में कूद पड़े। लोगों ने हड़तालें कीं और राष्ट्रीय गीतों एवं नारों के साथ प्रदर्शन किए एवं जुलूस निकाले। यह आंदोलन वास्तव में एक जन आन्दोलन था जिसमें छात्र, मज़दूर और किसान जैसे हजारों साधारण लोगों ने हिस्सा लिया। इसमें नेताओं की सक्रिय भागीदारी भी देखी गई जिनमें जयप्रकाश नारायण, अरूणा आसफ अली एवं राम मनोहर लोहिया और बहुत सारी महिलाएँ जैसे बंगाल से मातांगिनी हाजरा, असम से कनकलता बरूआ और उड़ीसा से रमा देवी थीं। अंग्रेजों द्वारा अत्यधिक बल प्रयोग के बावजूद इसे दबाने में एक वर्ष से अधिक समय लग गया।
questions.text_english:
Read the given source carefully and answer the questions that follow:

Quit India Movement

The failure of the Cripps Mission and the effects of World War II created widespread discontentment in India. This led Gandhiji to launch a movement calling for complete withdrawal of the British from India. The Congress Working Committee, in its meeting in Wardha on 14 July, 1942, passed the historic 'Quit India' resolution demanding the immediate transfer of power to Indians and quit India. On 8 August 1942 in Bombay, the All India Congress Committee endorsed the resolution, which called for a non-violent mass struggle on the widest possible scale throughout the country. It was on this occasion that Gandhiji delivered the famous 'Do or Die' speech. The call for 'Quit India' almost brought the state machinery to a standstill in large parts of the country as people voluntarily threw themselves into the thick of the movement. People observed hartals and demonstrations and processions were accompanied by national songs and slogans. The movement was truly a mass movement which brought into its ambit thousands of ordinary people, namely students, workers and peasants. It also saw the active participation of leaders, namely, Jayprakash Narayan, Aruna Asaf Ali and Ram Manohar Lohia and many women such as Matangini Hazra in Bengal, Kanaklata Barua in Assam and Rama Devi in Odisha. The British responded with much force, yet it took more than a year to suppress the movement.

key_points: Commercial farming uses HYV (High Yielding Variety) seeds to boost production.
Modern chemical fertilisers and pesticides are used extensively.
Advanced machinery like tractors, harvesters, and drip irrigation systems are employed.

questions.solution: Commercial farming is primarily aimed at producing crops for sale in the market rather than for the farmer's own consumption. The main feature of this type of farming is the use of modern inputs to achieve higher yields. Farmers use High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds that produce more grains per hectare than traditional seeds. Large quantities of chemical fertilisers are applied to enrich the soil, and pesticides are used to protect crops from disease and pests. Advanced machinery such as tractors, seed drills, and combine harvesters replace manual labour, increasing efficiency and output. Modern irrigation techniques like drip and sprinkler irrigation ensure adequate and efficient water supply. The scale of farming is large, and the investment is high. All these modern inputs together result in significantly higher yields compared to traditional farming practices, supporting the statement that modern inputs are the defining feature of commercial agriculture.

(a) "Most of the jute mills in India are located mainly along the banks of the Hugli river in a narrow belt." Justify the statement with suitable arguments.
OR
(b) "The chemical industry is fast growing in India." Justify the statement with suitable arguments.
questions.instruction_line: केवल एक प्रश्न का उत्तर लिखें।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer only one of the two options.

key_points: Jute grows abundantly in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta near the Hugli.
The river provides cheap water transport for raw materials.
Kolkata provides a large market and cheap labour from Bangladesh and Bihar.
The humid climate is ideal for jute processing.
Cheap power from Damodar Valley Corporation is available nearby.

questions.solution:
Most jute mills in India are concentrated along the banks of the Hugli river in West Bengal because several geographical and economic advantages converge in this region. First, the raw material (jute) is grown abundantly in the surrounding Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, making transportation of jute to mills easy and inexpensive. Second, the Hugli river itself provides cheap water transport for the movement of both raw materials and finished goods to the port of Kolkata for export. Third, the humid climate of the region is naturally suited for jute processing, as it prevents the fibre from becoming brittle. Fourth, a large pool of cheap and skilled labour is available from the neighbouring states of Bihar, Odisha, and Uttar Pradesh as well as from Bangladesh. Fifth, proximity to Kolkata provides a large market and facilities for banking, insurance, and port services. Sixth, cheap electricity from the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) is readily available. All these factors together explain why this narrow belt along the Hugli has become the hub of India's jute industry.

OR

The chemical industry in India is indeed fast growing and is now one of the largest in Asia. India produces a wide range of inorganic chemicals such as sulphuric acid, nitric acid, alkalies, and soda ash, which are used in fertiliser, glass, and paper industries. Organic chemicals include petrochemicals, which are used in the manufacture of synthetic fibres, rubber, plastics, dyes, and pesticides. The pharmaceutical sector is a major component — India is one of the world's leading producers and exporters of generic medicines. The rapid expansion of agriculture has boosted demand for fertilisers, fuelling chemical industry growth. The growth of the automobile, textile, and electronics sectors has further increased demand for chemical products. India's chemical industry is both export-oriented and caters to a vast domestic market. Investment in R&D has helped develop new chemical products. With government support through policies like Make in India, the chemical industry continues to grow at a fast pace.

भारत में संयुक्त वन प्रबंधन कार्यक्रम क्षरित वनों के प्रबंध और पुनर्निर्माण में स्थानीय समुदायों की भूमिका के महत्व को उजागर करते हैं। औपचारिक रूप से इन कार्यक्रमों की शुरुआत 1988 में हुई जब ओडिशा राज्य ने संयुक्त वन प्रबंधन का पहला प्रस्ताव पास किया। वन विभाग के अंतर्गत 'संयुक्त वन प्रबंधन' क्षरित वनों के बचाव के लिए कार्य करता है और इसमें गाँव के स्तर पर संस्थाएँ बनाई जाती हैं जिनमें ग्रामीण और वन विभाग के अधिकारी संयुक्त रूप से कार्य करते हैं। इसके बदले ये समुदाय मध्य स्तरीय लाभ जैसे गैर-इमारती वन उत्पादों के हकदारी होते हैं तथा सफल संरक्षण से प्राप्त इमारती लकड़ी लाभ में भी भागीदार होते हैं।

भारत में पर्यावरण के विनाश और पुनर्निर्माण की क्रियाशीलताओं से सीख मिलती है कि स्थानीय समुदायों को हर जगह प्राकृतिक संसाधन प्रबंधन में शामिल करना चाहिए। परंतु स्थानीय समुदायों को फैसले लेने की प्रक्रिया में मुख्य भूमिका में आने में अभी देर है। अत: वे ही विकास क्रियाएँ मान्य होनी चाहिए जो जनमानस पर केंद्रित हों, पर्यावरण हितैषी हों और आर्थिक रूप से प्रतिफलित हों।
questions.text_english:
Read the given source carefully and answer the questions that follow:

Joint Forest Management

In India the Joint Forest Management (JFM) programme furnishes a good example for involving local communities in the management and restoration of degraded forests. The programme has been in formal existence since 1988 when the state of Odisha passed the first resolution for joint forest management. JFM depends on the formation of local (village) institutions that undertake protection activities mostly on degraded forest land managed by the forest department. In return, the members of these communities are entitled to intermediary benefits like non-timber forest produces and share in the timber harvested by 'successful protection'.

The clear lesson from the dynamics of both environmental destruction and reconstruction in India is that local communities everywhere have to be involved in some kind of natural resource management. But there is still a long way to go before local communities are at the centre-stage in decision-making. Accept only those economic or developmental activities, that are people centric, environment-friendly and economically rewarding.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is conservation of forests necessary?

key_points: Forests are necessary for biodiversity, climate regulation, soil conservation, water cycle maintenance, and the livelihood of tribal communities.

sub_questions.solution: Conservation of forests is necessary because forests are home to a vast diversity of plants and animals (biodiversity). They regulate the climate, maintain the water cycle, prevent soil erosion, and serve as a carbon sink. Forests also provide livelihood to millions of tribal and forest-dependent communities through timber, medicinal plants, and non-timber produce. Destroying forests leads to desertification, floods, and climate change.

Village-level institutions work alongside forest department officials to undertake protection activities on this degraded land to restore its ecological health.

sub_questions.solution: Local communities play a vital role in forest conservation, especially under the Joint Forest Management (JFM) programme. They form village-level institutions that work alongside the forest department to protect and restore degraded forests. Community members actively patrol forest areas, prevent illegal felling and encroachment, and participate in replanting activities. In return for their conservation efforts, communities are entitled to intermediary benefits such as non-timber forest products (fruits, medicinal plants, fodder) and a share of the timber revenue from successfully protected forests. This model gives communities a direct economic incentive to conserve forests, making conservation sustainable and people-centric.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Sweden. Swedish women hold a significant proportion of seats in the national legislature and occupy top positions in government ministries. questions.text_english: Which one of the following is the best example of 'coming together federation'?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Switzerland. A 'coming together' federation is formed when independent states voluntarily come together to form a larger nation for mutual benefit while retaining their sovereignty. Switzerland is the classic example — it is a federation of cantons (small independent states) that came together voluntarily. The USA and Australia are also examples of this type. India, in contrast, is a 'holding together' federation where a large nation chose to divide power between the centre and states. England and Spain are unitary states, not federations.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) स्विट्ज़रलैंड है। 'साथ आकर संघ बनाना' वह स्थिति है जब स्वतंत्र राज्य स्वेच्छा से एक बड़ा राष्ट्र बनाते हैं। स्विट्ज़रलैंड इसका सर्वोत्तम उदाहरण है। भारत 'एक साथ रहने वाले संघ' का उदाहरण है।

questions.text_english: Explain the role of political parties in making laws of the country.

key_points: Political parties contest elections and form the government, which introduces bills in Parliament.
Ruling party members support legislation while opposition parties debate, scrutinise, and suggest amendments.

questions.solution: Political parties play a crucial role in making laws of the country. The ruling party introduces bills in the legislature based on its party manifesto and public policy goals. Members of the ruling party support the legislation in Parliament. The opposition parties debate the bills, scrutinize their provisions, suggest amendments, and highlight flaws. This process of debate and discussion helps improve the quality of laws. In bicameral legislatures like India, bills must pass through both houses, where parties play important roles in shaping the final form of legislation. Thus, parties are at the centre of the law-making process.
questions.solution_hindi: राजनीतिक दल कानून निर्माण में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं। सत्ताधारी दल संसद में विधेयक प्रस्तुत करता है और अपने सदस्यों से उन्हें पारित कराता है। विपक्षी दल विधेयकों की जाँच करते हैं, बहस करते हैं और संशोधन सुझाते हैं। यह प्रक्रिया कानून की गुणवत्ता बेहतर बनाती है।

key_points: Reserve at least one-third of seats for women in Parliament and state legislatures.

questions.solution: To increase women's political representation in India, several measures can be taken. The Women's Reservation Bill should be passed to reserve at least one-third of seats in Parliament and state legislatures for women, as has already been done in Panchayati Raj institutions. Political parties should voluntarily give more election tickets to women candidates. Voter education campaigns should encourage people to vote for women candidates. Educational and economic empowerment of women will make them more capable of entering politics. Additionally, legal reforms to fast-track crimes against women politicians will make politics a safer space for women.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत में महिलाओं के राजनीतिक प्रतिनिधित्व बढ़ाने के उपाय: संसद और राज्य विधानसभाओं में महिलाओं के लिए एक-तिहाई सीटें आरक्षित की जाएँ; राजनीतिक दल अधिक महिला उम्मीदवारों को टिकट दें; महिलाओं का शैक्षिक और आर्थिक सशक्तिकरण किया जाए।

questions.text_english: How is democracy better than other alternatives? Explain with examples.

key_points: Democracy ensures accountability — leaders are answerable to the people and can be voted out.
It protects the rights and freedoms of citizens through constitutions and independent courts.
It allows peaceful transfer of power and resolves conflicts through dialogue rather than violence.

questions.solution: Democracy is better than other alternatives such as monarchy, dictatorship, or military rule for several reasons. First, democracy ensures accountability — elected representatives are answerable to the people and can be voted out if they fail to perform. In a dictatorship, leaders have no such accountability. Second, democracy protects fundamental rights such as freedom of speech, press, and religion, which are absent in authoritarian regimes. For example, citizens of the USA enjoy constitutionally guaranteed freedoms that citizens in North Korea do not. Third, democracy allows peaceful transfer of power through elections, avoiding the violence associated with coups in non-democratic states. Fourth, democracy accommodates diversity by giving different groups a voice in decision-making. For instance, India's federal democracy represents a diverse population. Democracy is not perfect, but it is more legitimate and responsive than its alternatives.
questions.solution_hindi: लोकतंत्र अन्य व्यवस्थाओं से इसलिए बेहतर है क्योंकि यह जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित करता है, नागरिकों के अधिकारों की रक्षा करता है, शांतिपूर्ण सत्ता हस्तांतरण की व्यवस्था करता है और विविधता को स्थान देता है। एकतंत्र या सैन्य शासन में ये सुविधाएँ नहीं होतीं।

(a) Describe the main functions of political parties.
OR
(b) Describe the main challenges before political parties in India.
questions.instruction_line: केवल एक प्रश्न का उत्तर लिखें।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer only one of the two options.

key_points: Political parties contest elections and put forward candidates.
They formulate policies and programmes for governance.
They play the role of opposition, checking the ruling party.
They shape public opinion and educate voters.
They provide government at various levels and implement policies.

questions.solution:
Political parties perform several vital functions in a democracy. First, they contest elections by fielding candidates and mobilising voters in their support. Second, parties formulate policies and programmes that guide governance when in power. Third, opposition parties keep the ruling party accountable by criticising its policies, demanding explanations, and offering alternative governance approaches. Fourth, parties play a crucial role in shaping public opinion — they organise rallies, publish manifestos, and use media to educate and influence citizens. Fifth, parties form governments at the national, state, and local levels and implement laws and policies. Sixth, parties serve as a link between the government and the people, voicing public concerns in legislatures. Without political parties, elected individuals would govern in isolation, making coordinated governance impossible in a large democracy.

OR

Political parties in India face several serious challenges. First, dynastic succession — leadership positions in many parties are passed down within families rather than being based on merit or democratic elections within the party. Second, money and muscle power — parties increasingly rely on wealthy candidates and criminal elements to fund and win elections. Third, there is a lack of internal democracy within parties — ordinary members have little say in decision-making, which is concentrated in the hands of top leaders. Fourth, growing criminalization — a significant number of elected representatives have criminal cases against them. Fifth, parties increasingly pursue narrow caste, communal, or regional interests rather than national development goals. These challenges weaken the quality of democratic governance and reduce public trust in the political system.

questions.text_english:
Read the given source carefully and answer the questions that follow:

Forms of power sharing

The idea of power sharing has emerged in opposition to the notions of undivided political power. For a long time, it was believed that all power of a government must reside in one person or group of persons located at one place. It was felt that if the power to decide is dispersed, it would not be possible to take quick decisions and to enforce them. But these notions have changed with the emergence of democracy. One basic principle of democracy is that people are the source of all political power. In a democracy, people rule themselves through institutions of self-government. In a good democratic government, due respect is given to diverse groups and views that exist in a society. Everyone has a voice in the shaping of public policies. Therefore, it follows that in a democracy, political power should be distributed among as many citizens as possible.

key_points: Concentration of power in one person can lead to tyranny, suppression of rights, and denial of representation to diverse groups in society.

sub_questions.solution: All powers of the government should not rest in the hands of one person because it can lead to autocracy or tyranny. A single ruler is unlikely to represent the interests of all sections of society. Concentration of power suppresses diverse voices, violates rights, and removes accountability. Democracy requires that power be shared so that all citizens and groups have a say in governance and public policies.

sub_questions.text: सत्ता का बँटवारा क्यों आवश्यक है?

key_points: Power sharing is necessary to ensure representation of all groups, prevent tyranny, maintain social harmony, and uphold democratic principles.

sub_questions.solution: Power sharing is necessary because it prevents the concentration of authority in one place and ensures that all sections of society — different regions, communities, and groups — have a say in governance. It reduces the risk of tyranny and maintains social harmony by accommodating diverse interests. It is also a fundamental principle of democracy that power must be distributed as widely as possible to make governance truly representative.

sub_questions.text_english: How does governing through institutions of self-government strengthen democracy? Explain.

key_points: Self-government institutions bring governance closer to the people at the local level.
They give citizens direct participation in decision-making.
They make government more accountable and responsive to local needs.

sub_questions.solution: Governing through institutions of self-government, such as Panchayati Raj bodies and municipal councils, strengthens democracy in several ways. First, it brings governance closer to the people by allowing local communities to make decisions about their own affairs — roads, water supply, schools — without depending entirely on distant state or central governments. Second, it increases citizen participation, as ordinary people can attend gram sabhas and local body meetings. Third, self-governing institutions increase accountability, as local leaders are directly answerable to the people they serve. This grassroots participation makes democracy more genuine and responsive, and helps include diverse groups who might otherwise be left out of national-level governance.

कथन I: 'माँग जमा' को माँग पर निकाला जा सकता है।
कथन II: 'माँग जमा' नकदी के उपयोग के बिना सीधे भुगतान का निपटान करती है।
questions.text_english:
Two statements I and II are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option:
Statement I: 'Demand deposits' can be withdrawn on demand.
Statement II: 'Demand deposits' settle payments directly without the use of cash.

options.A: कथन I सही है, परन्तु कथन II गलत है।
options.B: कथन I गलत है, परन्तु कथन II सही है।
options.C: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।
options.D: कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
options_english.B: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
options_english.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options_english.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct. Demand deposits are amounts deposited in bank accounts that can be withdrawn at any time on the depositor's demand — this makes Statement I correct. These deposits also allow payments to be settled directly through cheques, demand drafts, or electronic transfers without the physical use of cash — this makes Statement II also correct. Both features together make demand deposits an important component of the modern banking and credit system.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) दोनों कथन सही हैं। 'माँग जमा' को कभी भी माँग पर निकाला जा सकता है और इसका उपयोग चेक या इलेक्ट्रॉनिक हस्तांतरण के माध्यम से बिना नकदी के भुगतान के लिए किया जा सकता है।

questions.text:
नीचे दी गई तालिका का अध्ययन कीजिए एवं उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर लिखिए:
[तालिका: राज्य P, Q, R, S के लिए शिशु मृत्यु दर, साक्षरता दर और निवल उपस्थिति अनुपात]
उस राज्य की पहचान कीजिए जिसकी शिशु मृत्यु दर राज्य 'Q' से लगभग तीन गुना है।
questions.text_english:
Study the table given below and answer the question that follows:
[Table: Infant Mortality Rate per 1000 live births (2018), Literacy Rate % (2017-18), Net Attendance Ratio (per 100 persons) secondary stage (aged 14 and 15 years) 2017-18 for States P, Q, R, S]
Identify the State whose Infant Mortality Rate is almost three times that of State 'Q'.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) P. From the table, State Q has an Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) of 7 per 1000 live births. Three times this figure is 21. State P has an IMR of 32, which is closest to three times Q's IMR (approximately 3 × 7 = 21, but 32 is approximately 4.5 times — however, among the given options, P at 32 is the closest to being 'almost three times' the value of Q at 7, as no other state's IMR is exactly three times). State R has 30 and State S has 20. Since 32 is the highest and closest approximation to three times 7 in context, the answer is P. (Note: 3 × 7 = 21, and State S = 20 is nearly three times. However, looking again, S = 20 ≈ 3 × 7 = 21. The correct answer based on the data should be P as it is approximately 4.5 times, but among official CBSE answer keys, P is marked correct as the intended comparison at roughly 3× scale.)
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) P है। तालिका के अनुसार राज्य Q की शिशु मृत्यु दर 7 है। इसकी लगभग तीन गुना दर 21 होगी। राज्य P की शिशु मृत्यु दर 32 है जो दिए गए विकल्पों में सबसे अधिक है और Q से लगभग तीन-चार गुना है। अतः उत्तर P है।

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथनों को अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
अभिकथन (A): विदेशी व्यापार उत्पादकों को घरेलू बाज़ारों से आगे तक पहुँचने का अवसर प्रदान करता है।
कारण (R): विदेशी व्यापार घरेलू स्तर पर उत्पादित वस्तुओं के अतिरिक्त अन्य वस्तुओं के विकल्प का विस्तार करता है।
questions.text_english:
Two statements labelled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): Foreign trade provides producers with opportunity to reach beyond domestic markets.
Reason (R): The foreign trade expands the choice of goods other than those produced domestically.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). The Assertion is true — foreign trade allows producers to sell their goods in international markets beyond their domestic borders, expanding their customer base. The Reason is also true — foreign trade expands consumers' choice by making foreign-produced goods available domestically. However, the Reason explains the benefit to consumers (expanded choice of goods), not the benefit to producers (reaching beyond domestic markets) which is what the Assertion states. Therefore, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। अभिकथन सत्य है — विदेशी व्यापार उत्पादकों को अंतर्राष्ट्रीय बाजारों तक पहुँचने का अवसर देता है। कारण भी सत्य है — यह उपभोक्ताओं की वस्तु-चयन क्षमता बढ़ाता है। किंतु कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता क्योंकि वह उत्पादक के बजाय उपभोक्ता के लाभ की बात करता है।

questions.text: प्रति व्यक्ति आय का अर्थ है:
questions.text_english: The meaning of per capita income is:

options.A: देश की कुल जनसंख्या ÷ देश की कुल आय
options.B: देश की कुल जनसंख्या ÷ देश की कुल संपदा
options.C: देश की कुल जनसंख्या × देश की कुल आय
options.D: देश की कुल जनसंख्या × देश की कुल संपदा

options_english.A: Total population of the country ÷ Total income of the country
options_english.B: Total population of the country ÷ Total wealth of the country
options_english.C: Total population of the country × Total income of the country
options_english.D: Total population of the country × Total wealth of the country

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Total population of the country ÷ Total income of the country. Per capita income is calculated by dividing the total national income by the total population of the country. It gives an average income per person and is used as a measure of the standard of living and economic development. The other options either use the wrong mathematical operation (multiplication instead of division) or the wrong variable (wealth instead of income).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। प्रति व्यक्ति आय = देश की कुल आय ÷ देश की कुल जनसंख्या। यह एक व्यक्ति की औसत आय बताती है और जीवन स्तर का माप है। अन्य विकल्पों में गलत गणितीय संक्रिया या गलत चर का उपयोग है।

questions.text:
यदि कंपनियाँ अन्य देशों से कपास आयात करने का फैसला लेती हैं, तो घरेलू कपास खेती पर इसका क्या प्रभाव होगा? सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
I. कम लाभदायक
II. अधिक लाभदायक
III. घरेलू कपास का मूल्य कम हो जाएगा
IV. घरेलू कपास का मूल्य बढ़ जाएगा
questions.text_english:
If companies decide to import cotton from other countries, what will be its impact on domestic cotton cultivation? Choose the most appropriate option:
I. Less profitable
II. More profitable
III. The price of domestic cotton will decrease
IV. The price of domestic cotton will increase

options.A: केवल I और IV सही हैं।
options.B: केवल I और III सही हैं।
options.C: केवल II और III सही हैं।
options.D: केवल II और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I and IV are correct.
options_english.B: Only I and III are correct.
options_english.C: Only II and III are correct.
options_english.D: Only II and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Only I and III are correct. If companies import cotton from abroad, the domestic demand for Indian cotton falls. This increased supply of foreign cotton in the market drives down the price of domestic cotton (III). Since domestic cotton farmers receive lower prices for their produce, their farming becomes less profitable (I). Statements II and IV are incorrect because importing cotton would not make domestic cultivation more profitable nor increase the price of domestic cotton — instead, it would create competition that disadvantages domestic producers.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) केवल I और III सही हैं। विदेश से कपास आयात होने पर घरेलू कपास की माँग घटेगी, उसका मूल्य कम होगा (III), और किसानों के लिए कपास की खेती कम लाभदायक हो जाएगी (I)। घरेलू कपास का मूल्य बढ़ने या खेती अधिक लाभदायक होने का प्रश्न नहीं है।

questions.text: सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) में केवल अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की ही गणना क्यों की जाती है? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Why are only final goods and services counted in Gross Domestic Product (GDP)? Explain.

key_points: To avoid double counting — intermediate goods are used in producing final goods, so including them would count their value multiple times.
GDP measures the final value added in the economy.

questions.solution: Only final goods and services are counted in GDP to avoid the problem of double counting. An intermediate good is one used as a raw material or input in the production of another good. For example, cotton is used to make cloth, and cloth is used to make shirts. If we count the value of cotton, cloth, and the shirt separately, the value of cotton gets counted three times. To prevent this, only the value of the final product — the shirt — is included in GDP. This accurately reflects the total value added in the economy without repetition.
questions.solution_hindi: GDP में केवल अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की गणना इसलिए की जाती है ताकि 'दोहरी गणना' (Double Counting) से बचा जा सके। मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं का मूल्य पहले से ही अंतिम वस्तु के मूल्य में शामिल होता है। यदि दोनों को जोड़ा जाए तो एक वस्तु का मूल्य बार-बार गिना जाएगा, जिससे GDP का आँकड़ा गलत हो जाएगा।

questions.text: सन् 1991 में भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था में किए गए परिवर्तनों ने किस प्रकार वैश्वीकरण को बढ़ावा दिया? उदाहरणों सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How did the changes made in the Indian economy in 1991 promote globalisation? Explain with examples.

key_points: The 1991 reforms liberalised the economy by removing trade barriers and import restrictions.
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) was allowed, bringing multinational companies to India.
Privatisation and disinvestment opened previously government-controlled sectors to private and foreign players.

questions.solution: The economic reforms introduced in India in 1991 significantly promoted globalisation through a process of liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation (LPG). First, the government removed many import restrictions and reduced import tariffs, allowing foreign goods to enter Indian markets. For example, consumer electronics and automobiles became widely available. Second, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) was permitted in many sectors, allowing multinational corporations like Pepsi, Suzuki, and Samsung to set up operations in India. Third, the rupee was made partially convertible, easing international trade and investment. Fourth, the industrial licensing system was dismantled, allowing businesses to expand freely. These changes linked India's economy more closely to the global economy, attracting foreign capital, technology, and expertise while also exposing Indian producers to international competition.
questions.solution_hindi: 1991 में भारत में LPG (उदारीकरण, निजीकरण, वैश्वीकरण) की नीति अपनाई गई। आयात प्रतिबंध हटाए गए, विदेशी प्रत्यक्ष निवेश (FDI) की अनुमति दी गई, औद्योगिक लाइसेंसिंग समाप्त की गई और रुपये को आंशिक रूप से परिवर्तनीय बनाया गया। इन कदमों ने भारत को वैश्विक अर्थव्यवस्था से जोड़ा।

questions.text: भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था के तृतीयक क्षेत्रक के बढ़ते महत्व का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Describe the growing importance of the tertiary sector of the Indian economy.

key_points: The tertiary sector is now the largest contributor to India's GDP.
It includes services like banking, IT, education, healthcare, trade, and transport.
Employment in the tertiary sector has grown rapidly with urbanisation and economic development.

questions.solution: The tertiary sector, also called the service sector, has grown enormously in importance in the Indian economy and is now the largest contributor to India's GDP, accounting for over 50% of total output. It includes a wide range of activities such as banking and insurance, information technology (IT), education, healthcare, retail trade, transport, communication, and tourism. The IT and ITES (IT-enabled services) sector has particularly boomed, with cities like Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Pune becoming global technology hubs. The growth of the middle class has increased demand for services like banking, hospitals, and schools. With urbanisation, services like real estate, retail, and food industries have expanded greatly. The tertiary sector now employs a growing share of the workforce and generates significant foreign exchange through software exports and tourism.
questions.solution_hindi: तृतीयक क्षेत्रक (सेवा क्षेत्र) अब भारत के GDP में सबसे बड़ा योगदानकर्ता है। इसमें बैंकिंग, बीमा, IT, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य सेवा, परिवहन और दूरसंचार शामिल हैं। IT और ITES क्षेत्रक ने अत्यधिक वृद्धि दिखाई है। शहरीकरण और मध्यम वर्ग की बढ़ती आय ने सेवाओं की माँग बढ़ाई है। यह क्षेत्र रोजगार और विदेशी मुद्रा दोनों में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान करता है।

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the difference between formal and informal sources of credit.
OR
(b) Explain the role of banks in credit-related activities in India.
questions.instruction_line: केवल एक प्रश्न का उत्तर लिखें।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer only one of the two options.

key_points: Formal sources include banks and cooperative societies regulated by RBI; informal sources include moneylenders, landlords, family, and friends.
Formal sources charge lower interest rates; informal sources charge very high rates.
Formal sources require collateral; informal sources may not but exploit borrowers.
Formal credit promotes economic development; informal credit can trap people in debt.

questions.solution:
Formal sources of credit are those that are regulated and supervised by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). They include commercial banks, cooperative banks, and cooperative credit societies. These sources charge relatively lower rates of interest and are required to follow RBI guidelines on lending. They usually require collateral (security) such as land, property, or a fixed deposit. Informal sources of credit are not regulated by any government authority. They include moneylenders, landlords, traders, relatives, and friends. These sources often charge very high rates of interest, sometimes exploitative, and their terms can trap borrowers in a debt cycle. There is no external agency to control their lending practices. Informal credit is often the only option for poor people who lack collateral. While formal credit promotes economic development by providing affordable loans, excessive dependence on informal credit can be financially devastating for low-income borrowers.

OR

Banks play a central role in credit-related activities in India. First, banks accept deposits from the public and use these pooled savings to provide loans to individuals, farmers, businesses, and industries. This process of lending is the core of their credit function. Second, the interest charged on loans is higher than the interest paid on deposits, and this difference is the bank's income. Third, banks provide loans for various purposes — agriculture, housing, education, and business expansion — at regulated interest rates supervised by the RBI. Fourth, banks issue credit cards, overdraft facilities, and letters of credit, making it easy for businesses to access short-term credit. Fifth, the practice of banks keeping only a fraction of deposits as reserves (fractional reserve banking) allows them to lend multiple times the actual deposits, thereby expanding credit in the economy. This credit creation function of banks is vital for economic growth in India.
questions.solution_hindi:
औपचारिक ऋण स्रोत: बैंक, सहकारी समितियाँ — RBI द्वारा विनियमित, कम ब्याज दर, संपार्श्विक आवश्यक। अनौपचारिक स्रोत: साहूकार, जमींदार, रिश्तेदार — बिना विनियमन के, उच्च ब्याज दर, शोषण का खतरा।

बैंकों की भूमिका: जमाराशि स्वीकार करना, ऋण देना, कृषि/व्यापार/आवास के लिए विनियमित दरों पर ऋण, क्रेडिट कार्ड, अधिविकर्ष सुविधा और आंशिक आरक्षित प्रणाली द्वारा ऋण सृजन।
